speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And I see that as a major risk for humanity.
zh: 而我认为这是对人类的重大风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second piece is my actual PDU.

speaker: Unknown
en: And having a lot of what's being discussed from a regulatory framework and
zh: 而目前从监管框架的角度被讨论的很多内容，以及

speaker: Unknown
en: Limitations on technology, et cetera, I think is like the modern road to serfdom.
zh: 对技术的种种限制等等，我认为就像是现代版的通往奴役之路。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like the concentration of technological capability, making it legal to do matrix multiplications is like the thing that will set us back to pre, not just industrial revolution, it's like pre-enlightenment capabilities.
zh: 这就像技术能力的集中，让矩阵乘法变得需要合法许可，这会把我们倒退到前——不只是工业革命之前，而是启蒙运动之前的能力水平。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 这是我能想到的对古典自由主义自由理念最大的攻击。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 但我要说的是，是的，有很多战略上的理由，比如说，设立这些审计机构等等，可以从法律角度等方面卸掉一些潜在的责任、罪责。

speaker: Unknown
en: The risk that I just don't think that any of, I think this is a problem with a lot of very smart people, especially when they've amassed large wealth and power, et cetera, is they think that they're going to be able to keep that.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 对绝大多数人来说，会导致与我描述的场景中我所担心的同等程度的农奴制，而对某些人来说，在一个中国 CCP 控制的

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.

en: If we had to all of a sudden have a drone incursion, the same level of, you know, what's happening in Ukraine, Russia, you know, coming up from Mexico.

en: And if you take Mexico, just say that they developed, you know, very naive drone technology and et cetera, like on the level of what's happening in Russia, Ukraine and Iran, how would we respond to that as a country if we had that coming up across our border?
zh: 如果你拿墨西哥来说，就假设他们开发出了，你知道的，非常初级的无人机技术等等，大概相当于俄罗斯、乌克兰和伊朗的水平，如果那种东西越过我们的边境过来，我们作为一个国家该怎么应对？

en: It doesn't matter.

en: We built our military to fight the last war.

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think we should have export controls?

speaker: Unknown
en: The exception to that is a little bit I think China has been a free rider of all of the benefits of a liberal free trade order for the rest of the world while they get to keep everything closed off.

speaker: Unknown
en: I am very, very happy and think that any government societies, people that want to embrace free exchange of ideas and trade and everything else, we should have a very vibrant economy and ecosystem, but totalitarian regimes should not be able to participate with that, especially in the case where they get all of the benefits of that and get to export themselves, you know, things that make them better able to have that totalitarian system keep up.

zh: 对我来说，政治光谱上最可怕的事，以及这一切被对待的方式，是它现在已经成为左右两派几乎团结一致的议题——反数据中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that is almost entirely a Chinese psyop.
zh: 我觉得这几乎完全是中国的心理战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I ask, why is it a Chinese SIOP being anti-data centers?
zh: 我能问一下，为什么反数据中心是中国的心理战？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it does increase.
zh: 因为它确实在增加。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm totally with you in the benefits of them.
zh: 我完全赞同你说的数据中心的好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Gavin Baker said how they're the greatest economic kind of needle mover for large parts of the country.
zh: Gavin Baker 说过，它们是全国大部分地区最了不起的经济推动因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess they see increased electricity prices, increased water prices, and ugly data centers in their backyard.
zh: 我猜他们看到的是电价上涨、水价上涨，以及后院里丑陋的数据中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is it a Chinese SIOP?
zh: 为什么这是中国的心理战？

speaker: Unknown
en: What am I not seeing?
zh: 我没看到什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, just on the ugly and all that, I totally am supportive.
zh: 嗯，就丑陋之类的说法，我完全支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to have beautification campaigns and really turn them into centerpieces of our society.
zh: 我们需要开展美化运动，真正把它们变成我们社会的中心杰作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if thousands of years from now, you know, future history looks and they should see these massive data centers, the really, really massive, impressive ones.
zh: 我觉得如果几千年后，你知道的，未来的历史回头看，他们应该看到这些巨型数据中心，那些真正非常庞大、令人印象深刻的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It should be like the Great Pyramids or something.
zh: 它们应该像大金字塔之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to dress them up to be the world wonders that they are technologically.
zh: 我们需要把它们装扮成它们在技术上所堪称的世界奇迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing from water usage and the amount of power they consume, et cetera, so much of the early information that went out by unsophisticated writers or things that are just patently false.
zh: 至于用水量和它们消耗的电力等等，早期流传出去的许多信息，来自不专业的写手，或者干脆就是彻头彻尾错误的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: A single in and out uses more water than water.
zh: 什么单个进出用水量比水还多。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the largest data centers in the United States and like it's golf courses are orders magnitude more.
zh: 你知道的，美国最大的数据中心，而像是高尔夫球场要多出几个数量级。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it's the meat, like these are closed loop, you know, liquid cold systems that, you know, you don't even want to use water in a lot of these cases.
zh: 就像是，你知道的，这些是闭环液冷系统，你知道的，在很多情况下你根本不想用水。

speaker: Unknown
en: So from the Chinese PSIOP perspective, they're not, to your point, they're not pacing the frontier.
zh: 所以从中国心理战的角度来看，正如你所说，他们没有守住前沿。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're adding, you know, gigawatts of...
zh: 他们在增加，你知道的，吉瓦级的……

speaker: Unknown
en: New electricity generation capacity, most of it being dirty.
zh: 新发电容量，其中大部分是脏电。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're building massive new data centers, horribly displacing people.
zh: 他们在建造巨大的新数据中心，极其粗暴地搬迁民众。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just irks me so much that we have the freedom in the Western world to criticize companies, governments, everything based on false information.
zh: 让我特别恼火的是，我们在西方世界有自由基于虚假信息去批评公司、政府、一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I love the freedom elements of that.
zh: 我热爱其中的自由元素。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it is a strategic disadvantage when China can just say, yeah, we're going to just bulldoze all these people's homes and do rolling blackouts wherever in order to serve the greater good of new training capacity.
zh: 但当中国可以说，对，我们就打算把这些人家的房子全推平，在随便哪里搞轮流停电，以便服务于新训练容量这个更大的善，这就成了一种战略劣势。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean this with the greatest of respect, but...
zh: 我说这话是怀着最大的敬意，但是……

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't understand how anyone thinks the US or Europe can beat China when they have no regulatory or policy restrictions.
zh: 我不明白，当他们没有任何监管或政策限制时，怎么会有人认为美国或欧洲能打败中国。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I mean, the UK, you can't put up a paper airplane without getting a permit.
zh: 我的意思是，在英国，你连一架纸飞机不放个许可证都放不起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like, we're fucked.
zh: 所以，我们完蛋了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you are getting there and you're becoming a European state in terms of the regulation and policy requirements.
zh: 但你正在走向那里，在监管和政策要求方面你正在变成一个欧洲国家。

speaker: Unknown
en: Am I wrong?
zh: 我说错了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Am I being overly negative?
zh: 我是不是太消极了？

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't get it.
zh: 如果我们增加发电能力，没有人说我们想从预留给人们住宅的能源中拿取能源。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're right.
zh: 你说得对。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the greatest advantage the US has in that regard is that there's still a lot of land, a lot of places that do not have all the same levels of restrictions.
zh: 我认为美国在这方面的最大优势是，仍然有大量的土地、大量的地方没有同样程度的限制。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't agree with a lot of things of most administrations of my lifetime, but
zh: 我不赞同我一生中大多数政府的很多事情，但是

speaker: Unknown
en: The current administration gets attacked for saying they're destroying our environments and destroying national parks, et cetera.
zh: 现任政府因说他们在破坏我们的环境、破坏国家公园等而受到攻击。

speaker: Unknown
en: The vast, vast majority, 90 plus percent, I don't know the exact numbers, of national federal land is just open, empty desert in the West that is not part of a national park or anything.
zh: 绝大多数，90% 以上，我不知道确切的数字，国家联邦土地只是开放的、空旷的西部沙漠，不属于国家公园或任何东西的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the fact that there are so many restrictions to utilizing BLM land for building data centers where it's literally hundreds of miles from any populated area.
zh: 而事实上，在利用 BLM 土地建设数据中心方面有如此多的限制，而那里 literally 距离任何人口聚居区都有数百英里。

speaker: Unknown
en: My great state of Nevada has plentiful geothermal, solar, all these green energy technologies, and we could build nuclear and other things in the middle of the desert where it won't impact anyone, and that there's restrictions to that.
zh: 我伟大的内华达州有丰富的地热、太阳能，所有这些绿色能源技术，我们可以在沙漠中间建核电站和其他东西，不会影响任何人，而这方面居然有限制。

speaker: Unknown
en: is completely absurd to me.
zh: 在我看来完全荒谬。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I will say there has been some political will and push to solve these things, but literally just in the past year, you have Republican governors and other politicians that at least had part of their platform to be pro-growth and all of these things backing away because they see from their own political base being anti-data center based on completely false premises.
zh: 我要说，确实有一些解决这些问题的政治意愿和推动力，但仅仅在过去一年里，你有共和党州长和其他政客，他们政纲的一部分至少是支持增长和所有这些东西的，却因为看到自己的政治基本盘基于完全错误的前提而反数据中心而退缩了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the points I want to go back to that you brought up was that people would have higher electricity costs.
zh: 我想回到你提出的一个观点，那就是人们的电费会更高。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the most basic supply and demand.
zh: 这是最基本的供需关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we increase generation capacity and no one's saying we want to be taking energy from what's reserved for people's homes.
zh: 如果我们增加发电容量——而且没有人会说我们想从预留给民宅的能源里拿走一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the regulatory problems I see is power companies have to have this offer of...
zh: 我看到的一个监管问题是，电力公司必须有这种提供的……

speaker: Unknown
en: Energy availability that is baked into the cost and capabilities for everyone.
zh: 能源可用性，它是为所有人内置到成本和能力中的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is absolutely zero cases where a data center could be potentially pulling power from anything that's already been allocated.
zh: 绝对没有任何情况是数据中心可能从任何已经分配出去的东西中获取电力的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's just an impossibility.
zh: 所以那根本不可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all these data centers that are getting built right now are coming with generation capacity that covers their own use and beyond that.
zh: 而现在正在建设的所有这些数据中心都自带覆盖其自身使用乃至超出之外的发电能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're just not allowing them to hook up to the grid.
zh: 而我们只是不允许它们接入电网。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where they could actually be lowering the prices for everyone.
zh: 而它们实际上本可以降低所有人的价格。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you've got people on the power company side, like they're lobbying against new generation capacity, because that will actually, you know, market forces will, more capacity will decrease prices, which would be good for consumers.
zh: 然后你还有电力公司那边的人，他们在游说反对新的发电能力，因为那实际上，你知道，市场力量会，更多的容量会降低价格，而这对消费者是有利的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a very wonky market.
zh: 所以这是一个非常怪异的市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: What percentage of data centers that are planned will be completed, do you think?
zh: 你认为计划中的数据中心有多少比例会建成？

speaker: Unknown
en: From the major providers, I think I would say that the capacity that they have planned, they may be in different locations.
zh: 从主要提供商来看，我想我会说，他们计划的容量，它们可能位于不同的地点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you've had some local communities that have successfully stopped facilities going in there, but then those data centers just move.
zh: 我的意思是，你有一些当地社区成功地阻止了设施进驻，但那些数据中心只是搬走。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think a year ago, the major data center builders and operators were thinking that the political problems were as bad as they were.
zh: 我不认为一年前，主要的数据中心建设商和运营商就想到政治问题会像现在这么严重。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there is a lot more effort being put into education in those communities now, which I think will turn the tide a bit.
zh: 所以现在在这些社区的教育上投入了更多的努力，我认为这会稍微扭转局势。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I mean, it's also just going to mean that those data centers move to locales that aren't going to have those problems as well.
zh: 但我的意思是，这也只会意味着那些数据中心会搬到不会有那些问题的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like I said, we've got large tracts of land that can support it.
zh: 就像我说的，我们有大片可以支撑它的土地。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm not too worried that it's going to be like an existential threat and capacity build out.
zh: 所以我不太担心这会成为一个对容量建设的生存威胁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, of course, there's space if Elon's successful.
zh: 当然，还有太空，如果 Elon 成功的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you believe that space is a viable alternative, truly?
zh: 你真的相信太空是一个可行的替代方案吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is it conference talk and lip service to justify a market cap?
zh: 还是说那只是会议上的空谈和为市值辩护的口头承诺？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think something can start as one thing and turn into something else.
zh: 我认为一件事可以以一个东西开始，然后变成另一个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would never, ever bet against Elon.
zh: 我永远不会、永远不会赌 Elon 输。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I primarily bet for Elon.
zh: 我的意思是，我主要是赌 Elon 赢。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you asked me a year ago, I just would not have thought that there would be a good reason for it in the near term because it's going to be cheaper, easier, et cetera, to build on land.
zh: 如果你一年前问我，我根本不会认为在近期会有一个好的理由，因为在陆地上建设会更便宜、更容易等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think there's great alternative technologies.
zh: 我也认为有很好的替代技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: A company we're partnered with, and I'm good friends with, the CEO is a company called Panthalossa that's building ocean-based data centers, basically a very interesting pumped hydro solution in the middle of the ocean.
zh: 一家我们与之合作、我和其 CEO 是好朋友的公司，是一家叫 Panthalossa 的公司，正在建设海洋数据中心，基本上是在海洋中间的一个非常有趣的抽水蓄能解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there are alternatives that don't require going into space, I think long-term.
zh: 所以我认为，长期来看，有不需要进入太空的替代方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: Part of the reason I'm a long-term big believer in space data centers is I just think we're going to need to have a space economy for humanity to live up to its long-term potential.
zh: 我长期看好太空数据中心的部分原因是，我只是认为人类要实现其长期潜力，我们将需要有一个太空经济。

speaker: Unknown
en: Love that.
zh: 爱了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally agree.
zh: 完全同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll never bet against Elon.
zh: 我永远不会赌 Elon 输。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we think about like the cost of intelligence being tied to the cost of energy, how should we think about energy as a bottleneck moving forwards?
zh: 如果我们思考智能的成本与能源的成本绑定在一起，向前看我们应该如何思考能源作为一个瓶颈？

speaker: Unknown
en: To what extent is it?
zh: 它在多大程度上是？

speaker: Unknown
en: We mentioned policy and regulation being a core bottleneck.
zh: 我们提到过政策和监管是一个核心瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is energy a bottleneck moving forwards or less than people consider?
zh: 向前看能源是不是一个瓶颈，还是比人们认为的更不重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's two pieces to it.
zh: 我认为这有两个部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, one, Positron is trying to deliver more compute, more capabilities per watt per megawatt.
zh: 我是说，第一，Positron 正在尝试交付更多的算力，每瓦、每兆瓦更多的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you know, sort of on our base case, we can turn what you would have spent 500 megawatts with NVIDIA equipment and do that 100 megawatt.
zh: 所以，你知道，按照我们的基准情况，你原本用 NVIDIA 设备要花 500 兆瓦的东西，我们可以用 100 兆瓦做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think that's actually going to mean that you're only going to build 100 megawatt facility.
zh: 我不认为这实际上会意味着你只会建一座 100 兆瓦的设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're still going to build the maximum amount of compute that you can.
zh: 你还是会建你能建的最多算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're just getting more tokens, more intelligence per joule.
zh: 你只是得到了更多的 token、每焦耳更多的智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if I go back to the long-term thinking, you know, I think assuming humanity continues for hundreds, thousands of years, everything turns into an energy problem.
zh: 所以如果回到长期思考，你知道，我认为假设人类再延续几百年、几千年，一切都会变成一个能源问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can go back thousands of years and just look at the progression of mankind.
zh: 你可以回溯几千年，只看人类的进程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fundamentally, that is a perfect track of our ability to produce and use energy, discovery of fire up to, you know, nuclear power plants.
zh: 从根本上说，那就是一条对我们生产和利用能源能力的完美追踪，从发现火一直到，你知道，核电站。

speaker: Unknown
en: The simple tongue-in-cheek answer to your question is all progress is gated by energy.
zh: 对你的问题一个简单带点调侃的答案是：所有的进步都被能源所限制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even if there's energy available, it may not be economical and so it won't be done.
zh: 而且即使有能源可用，它可能不经济，所以就不会去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So actually I would say the bigger limiter than just saying that energy, like our ability to build and produce energy.
zh: 所以实际上我会说，比单纯说能源更大的限制因素——比如我们建设和生产能源的能力——

speaker: Unknown
en: We've got plenty of technologies and capability to do it.
zh: 我们已经有足够多的技术和能力去做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say we have got way more economic limitations.
zh: 我会说我们有更多的经济层面的限制。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, how much debt is the world willing to take on to build out everything over the next couple of years?
zh: 就像，未来几年全世界愿意背负多少债务来建设这一切？

speaker: Unknown
en: It ties into energy, it ties into the infrastructure itself, et cetera.
zh: 这与能源挂钩，与基础设施本身挂钩，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think economics is a much easier sort of scapegoat.
zh: 所以我认为经济是一个更容易找到的替罪羊。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, people are already very concerned by the levels of debt being taken out in the debt cycle.
zh: 我是说，人们已经非常担心债务周期中被举借的债务水平了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think their concerns are justified and then do you share them?
zh: 你认为他们的担忧是合理的吗？然后你自己也有同感吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we've got a major sovereign debt problem that masks a huge amount of second and third order elements in the financial system.
zh: 我认为我们有一个重大的主权债务问题，它掩盖了金融体系中大量的二阶和三阶因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just the inflationary consequences of government that can print infinite amounts of its own currency.
zh: 单说一个能无限印刷自己货币的政府所带来的通胀后果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the fact that we are, as we're already seeing the treasuries and the greater bond markets, that there is greater and greater perceived risk of the most, quote unquote, risk-free asset.
zh: 以及这样一个事实：正如我们已经在国债和更大的债券市场上看到的那样，那种最所谓的“无风险资产”的感知风险越来越大。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think will trickle down to all elements of the financial system.
zh: 我认为这会渗透到金融体系的所有环节。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when people worry about Oracle's debt and credit rating, I'm like, I believe in Oracle's business model and ability to execute and do everything a whole lot more than United States government.
zh: 所以当人们担心 Oracle 的债务和信用评级时，我的反应是，我对 Oracle 的商业模式和执行能力、做好所有事情的信心，远大于对美国的政府的信心。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just the United States government can issue its own currency and also has.
zh: 只不过是政府能发行自己的货币，而且还有——

speaker: Unknown
en: Guns and nukes to take tax revenue.
zh: 枪和核武器来征收税款。

speaker: Unknown
en: So my biggest economic concern there is that there will be a more acute specific crisis that arises out of the compounding of national debt leading to devaluation of the currency that has all of the consequences downstream rather than like, I'm really not worried about any of the companies in the AI debt stream not hitting their revenue targets.
zh: 所以我在那里最大的经济担忧是，会爆发一个更急剧的具体危机，源于国债的复利累积，导致货币贬值，并带来所有下游的后果，而不是说——我真的不担心 AI 债务链条上的任何一家公司达不到它们的营收目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if the past
zh: 就像如果过去

speaker: Unknown
en: Three, four years have shown we're accelerating every aspect of these businesses in terms of revenue profits and how they are improving the productivity and value downstream.
zh: 三四年已经表明，我们正在加速这些业务的每一个方面，包括营收、利润，以及它们如何在下游提升生产力和价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm jumping around, but fuck it.
zh: 我在跳来跳去，但管他呢。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I was doing the research, I was reading about KV caching and compression as part of this.
zh: 我在做功课时，我在读关于 KV 缓存和压缩的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was honestly getting lost, but I was intrigued and digging deeper and deeper.
zh: 老实说我被搞糊涂了，但我被吸引了，越挖越深。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, why did I not know this before?
zh: 然后我想，为什么我以前不知道这个？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I don't think many will know this.
zh: 所以我认为很多人不会知道这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: What should we know about KV caching?
zh: 关于 KV 缓存我们应该知道些什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is it important?
zh: 它为什么重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you explain it to me a little bit?
zh: 你能给我解释一下吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's always, I would say, a give and take relationship with innovation.
zh: 我认为，创新总是存在一种此消彼长的关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess one element I'll just have to explain to make all this clear is the concept of a sequence.
zh: 我想有一个要素我得先解释一下，才能把这一切讲清楚，那就是序列的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: I kind of already talked about a token, you know, a token effectively as part of the training process.
zh: 我其实已经讲过 token 了，你知道，token 实际上是训练过程的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: When any of these big model apps are developing a new model, they have a vocabulary that they define.
zh: 当这些大模型应用中的任何一个在开发新模型时，它们会定义一个词表。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they take their big giant corpus and they do some statistical work to figure out what is the best encoding method to take all of the text in this and break it into chunks that get reused frequently to have things be more efficient.
zh: 所以它们会拿它们的超大语料库，做一些统计工作，来搞清楚什么是最好的编码方法，把其中所有的文本切分成会被频繁复用的块，让事情更高效。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you end up doing is if you took an English dictionary, you'll find that there are common prefixes and suffixes and groupings of words.
zh: 你最终做的事情是，如果你拿一本英语词典，你会发现有常见的词缀、后缀和词的组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you just try to think of how would I best compress this if I just had symbols for these prefixes, suffixes, et cetera, compress this into a thing.
zh: 如果你试着想：如果我用符号来表示这些词缀、后缀等，我怎样能最好地把它压缩成一个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And basically what ends up happening is a token
zh: 基本上最终发生的事情是一个 token

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're using ChatGPT and you see text streaming out, if that's going particularly slow or you have quite a keen eye, you'll see that it's portions of words that come out at times, sometimes a full word, sometimes a small fraction of word, and each of those little flashes that you see is a token.
zh: 如果你用的是 ChatGPT,看到文字流式输出，如果速度特别慢或者你眼神足够敏锐，你会看到有时出来的是词的一部分，有时是完整的词，有时是一个词的一小部分，你看到的每一次这样的小闪烁就是一个 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: And roughly speaking, a token is equivalent to a half to like 75% of a word on average in large English corpuses.
zh: 粗略地说，在大型英文语料库中，一个 token 平均相当于半个到 75% 个词。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's token.
zh: 这就是 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: A sequence, or the thing that builds up to being context in a model, is the grouping of all those tokens in N order.
zh: 序列，也就是在模型中构建成上下文的东西，是所有这些 token 按 N 顺序的组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what happens when you're running an inference?
zh: 那么当你运行推理时会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You've given a prompt.
zh: 你给了一个 prompt。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have, what is the capital of France as your input prompt?
zh: 你的输入 prompt 是“法国的首都是什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: That is tokenized.
zh: 它被 token 化了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is four, five, six tokens that go into the model.
zh: 那是四、五、六个 token,进入模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you do inference, it's going to say the capital of France is Paris and the City of Lights, you know, some thing after that.
zh: 当你做推理时，它会输出“法国的首都是巴黎，光之城”，后面还有一点别的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when you have that entire sequence, when Transformers originally came out, for every token that was generated, you were doing the computation for generating all of those tokens, including the ones that you've already processed.
zh: 当你拥有整个序列时，在 Transformers 最初问世的时候，每生成一个 token,你都在为生成所有这些 token 做计算，包括那些你已经处理过的 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, clever, I would say kind of obvious based on, you know, all of the developments in the past of computer history, but wasn't done initially, was that, well, you don't actually have to redo the compute of the things that you've already, you know, had as inputs and what you've already generated in this turn.
zh: 而且，你知道，很聪明，基于计算机历史上过去所有的发展，我会说这有点显而易见，但最初并没有这么做，那就是：其实你不必为那些你已经有过的输入以及在这一轮中已经生成的内容重新做计算。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the KV cache was born where...
zh: 于是 KV cache 就诞生了，其中……

speaker: Unknown
en: Within the model, there's these two matrices called K and V, keys and values.
zh: 在模型内部，有两个矩阵叫 K 和 V,即 keys 和 values。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those matrices are fully based on the prompt and whatever is generated during a turn.
zh: 这些矩阵完全基于 prompt 以及一轮中生成的任何内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so by actually storing those two matrices, you can avoid having to redo computation at the cost of now having to store this thing in memory.
zh: 所以通过实际存储这两个矩阵，你可以避免重做计算，代价是现在必须把这个东西存储在内存里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's, you know, the simple example, you know, very, very small, hundreds of kilobytes of data.
zh: 那是一个简单的例子，非常非常小，几百 KB 的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the thing is that these things grow with the sequence length.
zh: 但问题是这些东西会随着序列长度增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the interesting thing is that for the attention mechanism, the compute per token grows quadratically with the sequence length.
zh: 但有趣的是，对于注意力机制，每个 token 的计算量随序列长度呈二次方增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're having to spend more and more compute quadratically.
zh: 所以你不得不花费越来越多的计算，呈二次方增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's an exponential curve as sequence length grows.
zh: 所以随着序列长度增长，那是一条指数曲线。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you store that as just your KNV, that's just a linear growth.
zh: 但当你把它存储为你的 KNV 时，那只是线性增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: What KV caching does is means that you don't have to do that compute, which gets very expensive very quickly at the expense of needing to store these things.
zh: KV caching 的作用是意味着你不必做那种计算——那种计算会很快变得非常昂贵——代价是需要存储这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Storing that is a complexity in itself because that's a unique KV cache for every single user that you're serving.
zh: 存储本身就是一件复杂的事，因为你服务的每一个用户都有一个独特的 KV cache。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it comes questions of how long do you want to keep that for?
zh: 于是就有了这样的问题：你想把它保留多久？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how do you manage all of that in a large system?
zh: 以及在一个大型系统中你如何管理这一切？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does it mean then when we hear about compression and uncompression of KV caching and potential entropy within the system?
zh: 那么当我们听到 KV caching 的压缩和解压缩以及系统内潜在的熵时，这意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's two different forms of oppression, a couple more than that, but the two main ones.
zh: 所以有两种不同形式的压迫，其实不止两种，但主要的是这两种。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one is quantization.
zh: 第一种是量化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you've got each of your values, be it your weights, your KV caches, activations stored in a particular data type.
zh: 如果你的每一个值，无论是权重、KV cache 还是激活值，都以某种特定的数据类型存储。

speaker: Unknown
en: So before the machine learning revolution, you know, most of the world's computation was done in FP32.
zh: 在机器学习革命之前，你知道，世界上大部分计算都是用 FP32 做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have 32 bits to represent a floating point number, and that's broken into mantissa and exponents.
zh: 你有 32 个比特来表示一个浮点数，它被分成尾数和指数。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it was pretty quickly realized that having 32 bits of precision was super overkill for the things that you're wanting to represent.
zh: 很快人们就意识到，对于你想要表示的东西来说，32 比特的精度实在太过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, it's both cost more from a storage and computational perspective than lower precision.
zh: 而且，你知道，从存储和计算的角度来看，它都比低精度成本更高。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we went to FP16, you know, Google developed BF16, you know, a little rejiggering of those bits.
zh: 于是我们到了 FP16,你知道，Google 开发了 BF16,你知道，对这些比特做了一点重新调整。

speaker: Unknown
en: Went to FP8, now we're at FP4 in popular systems.
zh: 到了 FP8,现在流行的系统已经到了 FP4。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we've been reducing the precision quite quickly, but that does lead to, for lack of a better word, some brain loss when these models run, just because you are now trying to encode the same information into fewer bits.
zh: 所以我们一直在相当快地降低精度，但这确实导致，找不到更好的词的话，模型运行时的一些“脑力损失”，只是因为你现在试图把同样的信息编码进更少的比特里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's been a lot of interesting schemes to say, okay, I'm going to take this group of FP16 values, or BF16 values,
zh: 于是有很多有趣的方案说，好，我要取这一组 FP16 值，或 BF16 值，

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm going to quantize those.
zh: 然后我要对它们做量化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm going to, you know, use a truncate and rounding that down to, let's say, int four values.
zh: 所以我要，你知道，用截断和舍入把它们降到，比如说，int4 值。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now you actually saved 75% of your total size of that group of values.
zh: 所以现在你实际上省下了那组值总大小的 75%。

speaker: Unknown
en: You shrunk that down from 16 bits to four bits.
zh: 你把它从 16 比特缩小到了 4 比特。

speaker: Unknown
en: But just doing that naively will mean that on a lot of benchmark scores, you'll have them get 20, 30% worse.
zh: 但只是朴素地这么做意味着在许多基准测试分数上，你会让它们变差 20%、30%。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you get that 75% savings in space, but you kind of lobotomize the model.
zh: 所以你在空间上省了 75%,但你在某种程度上给模型做了脑叶切除。

speaker: Unknown
en: But advanced quantization techniques actually say, okay, these 16 values, I'm able to have a shared bias and a multiplier for it.
zh: 但先进的量化技术实际上说，好，这 16 个值，我可以为它们设置一个共享的偏置和一个乘数。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say for those 16 now int4 or fp4 values,
zh: 比如说对于那 16 个现在的 int4 或 fp4 值，

speaker: Unknown
en: You store one new FP16 value that gets applied to all of those at compute time.
zh: 你存储一个新的 FP16 值，它会在计算时应用到所有这些值上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you get a 75% compression on all those values at the cost of now adding to add one new FP16.
zh: 所以你在所有这些值上得到 75% 的压缩，代价是现在要额外添加一个新的 FP16。

speaker: Unknown
en: And basically the state of the art here is you're able to get things compressed
zh: 基本上，这里的最先进水平是你能够把东西压缩

speaker: Unknown
en: From, you know, FP16, 16 bits per value down to like four and a half bits per value.
zh: 从 FP16 的每个值 16 比特压缩到大约每个值四个半比特。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that can be applied to weights, the actual parameters and model that could be applied to the KV caches, but there's no such thing as free launch.
zh: 这可以应用于权重，也就是模型的实际参数，也可以应用于 KV 缓存，但天下没有免费的午餐。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'd still have some lobotomy, but thankfully it's kept within like 1% of a unquantized model.
zh: 你还是会有一些「脑叶切除」式的损失，但幸运的是，它保持在未量化模型的 1% 以内。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is KV caching the hardest element of building that inference infrastructure?
zh: KV 缓存是构建推理基础设施中最难的部分吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is it, you name it, latency SLOs or load spikes or anything else that we could come up with?
zh: 于是这就变成了一个非常有趣的权衡：好吧，你想把加速器内存中的多少分配给权重？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that the hardest?
zh: 那是最难的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do we not see that we should see?
zh: 有什么是我们看不到但应该看到的？

speaker: Unknown
en: You can run a service and do something without having KV caching at all.
zh: 你完全可以在完全没有 KV 缓存的情况下运行一个服务并做事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to economics and performance and everything else wise is going to be much worse.
zh: 但在经济性、性能以及其他所有方面都会差得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: The dark arts and magic with it is the workloads that the industry so far has found the most valuable happen to be very, very highly cacheable.
zh: 这其中的黑暗艺术和魔法在于，迄今为止业界发现最有价值的工作负载，恰好是非常、非常高度可缓存的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Semi-Analysis has their AgentX benchmark and suite of test data based on taking a whole lot of Claude code sessions and having dozens to hundreds of turns in those Claude sessions with sub-agents and everything else.
zh: 所以 Semi-Analysis 有他们的 AgentX 基准测试和测试数据套件，其方法是把大量 Claude code 会话拿来，这些 Claude 会话中有几十到几百轮对话，还有子智能体等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what they found is over these massive number of interactions of these like real traced code generation, agentic coding sessions, about 96% of all the tokens that go through these entire sessions are cached.
zh: 他们发现，在这些真实的、被追踪记录的代码生成智能体编码会话的大量交互中，贯穿这些整个会话的所有 token 里大约有 96% 是被缓存的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you know your workload is going to have this extremely high caching rate where you're going to be reusing the same tokens again and again, that drastically shifts the importance of how you can retrieve those caches because these things get to be very, very large.
zh: 所以如果你知道你的工作负载会有这种极高的缓存命中率，你会反复复用相同的 token，这就极大地改变了「如何检索这些缓存」的重要性，因为这些缓存会变得非常、非常庞大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we have gone into trillions of parameters.
zh: 比如我们已经进入了数万亿参数的规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we just take the GPT-4 got leaked as 1.8 trillion parameter model.
zh: 如果我们拿 GPT-4 来说，它泄露为 1.8 万亿参数模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, assuming that that is in for quantized and rounding down a little bit, you know, that's 900 gigabytes of data size for the model weights.
zh: 现在，假设它是未量化（for quantized）的，并且稍微向下取整，你知道，模型权重的数据大小大约是 900 GB。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we take like the high expectations of like Claude Fable, you know, that's a 10 trillion parameter model.
zh: 如果我们按照对 Claude Fable 之类的高预期来看，你知道，那是一个 10 万亿参数的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So around five terabytes of model weights.
zh: 所以大约是 5 TB 的模型权重。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the crazy thing is at these long context links for these size models, you have the individual user sessions being in the, let's say in the hundred gigabyte range.
zh: 但疯狂的是，在这种规模模型的长上下文长度（links）下，单个用户会话会达到，比方说，几百 GB 的量级。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with just 50 users on your service, the user context, just those individual sessions end up being greater than the model weights that you're trying to store.
zh: 所以只要你的服务上有 50 个用户，用户上下文，仅仅这些单独的会话，就会超过你试图存储的模型权重。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Claude and OpenAI have a whole lot more than 50 users.
zh: 而 Claude 和 OpenAI 的用户远不止 50 个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it becomes a really interesting trade-off of, okay, how much of the accelerator memory do you want to dedicate to weights?
zh: 所以这就变成了一个非常有趣的权衡:好吧,你想把多少加速器内存 dedic给权重?

speaker: Unknown
en: Which you need to process every single token generated and you want that to be as fast as possible because that sets your SLO, that sets the token latency.
zh: 权重是你处理每一个生成 token 都需要的，而且你希望它尽可能快，因为这决定了你的 SLO，决定了 token 延迟。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you don't have their KVCaches persistent, you're actually losing a huge amount of efficiency because that was work that you didn't have to actually repeat.
zh: 但如果你不让他们的 KV 缓存持久化，你实际上会损失大量的效率，因为那是你本来不必重复做的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it saves you as an operator money more than anything at some level.
zh: 所以在某种程度上，这首先是为运营者省钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, having users' kvcaches be persistent will give some level of speed improvements that the user perceives, but it's mostly an economics thing for the service provider, where if you can return to them and use those tokens again and again, that saves you money as an operator massively.
zh: 你知道，让用户的 KV 缓存持久化，会给用户带来一定程度的、用户能感知到的速度提升，但这主要是对服务提供商来说的经济性问题——如果你能回到那些缓存并一次次复用那些 token，作为运营者，这会极大地为你省钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally get that.
zh: 完全理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: It saves us money because we don't have to use as much compute, but then it's harder from a memory challenge perspective.
zh: 它为我们省钱，因为我们不必使用那么多的算力，但从内存挑战的角度来看，这就更难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about the right logical next step then?
zh: 那么你认为正确的逻辑下一步是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you appreciate the importance of saving on compute, but the challenge of memory with KV caching, what's the answer then?
zh: 如果你认可节省算力的重要性，同时也看到了 KV 缓存带来的内存挑战，那答案是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: That we just have bigger and bigger memory stacks on chip?
zh: 是我们在芯片上堆越来越大的内存堆栈吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that look like?
zh: 那会是什么样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: The most common deployed solution and the vast majority of inferences out there are taking place on GPUs followed up by TPUs and a couple other devices.
zh: 目前最常见的部署方案，以及市面上绝大多数的推理，都是在 GPU 上进行的，其次是 TPU 和其他一些设备。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the most common paradigm today is you've got your GPU accelerator memory that is primarily responsible for holding the weights and you will keep some number of user sessions on there, the ones that you're actively processing.
zh: 但今天最常见的范式是：你有 GPU 加速器内存，它主要负责保存权重，你会在上面保留一定数量的用户会话，即你正在积极处理的那些。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the larger group of users has a tiered hierarchy.
zh: 但更大的那部分用户群体则有一个分层层级结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you'll have users that were around, say, in the past couple of seconds, but haven't returned, don't have an active request.
zh: 所以你会有些用户，比方说，在过去几秒钟里还在，但还没有回来，没有活跃请求。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's residing in host memory.
zh: 那些就驻留在主机内存中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And let's say that's on the order of anywhere 4 to 10x more memory on the host than in the accelerators.
zh: 比方说，主机上的内存比加速器上的内存多 4 到 10 倍左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you'll be able to store more of those there.
zh: 这样你就能在那里存储更多这样的会话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then if someone hasn't been around in a couple of minutes, maybe a couple of hours, that's going to be stored in even further away memory.
zh: 然后如果某个人已经好几分钟没出现了，也许好几个小时，那就会被存储在更远的内存里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that could be in NVMe, so flash storage, so a lot slower, but a lot larger capacity on that host.
zh: 那可能是在 NVMe 上，也就是闪存存储，慢得多，但在那台主机上容量大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be in flash storage on a network attached drive.
zh: 也可能是在网络附加硬盘的闪存存储上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And eventually, I bet the ChatGPT sessions that I had six months ago, somewhere residing on a disk, slow SSD or somewhere.
zh: 最终，我敢打赌，我六个月前的那些 ChatGPT 会话，正存放在某个磁盘上，某个慢速 SSD 或某个地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a data center, but it would be dumb for them to use expensive memory to store that.
zh: 在某个数据中心里，但如果他们用昂贵的内存来存那个就太蠢了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that tiering is the norm, but that introduces a huge amount of complexity of how do you decide when and where you're going to store something for your massive number of users?
zh: 所以这种分层是常态，但这引入了大量的复杂性：对于你数量庞大的用户，你如何决定在什么时候、在哪里存储某些东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say our solution, kind of how we're trying to go about it, both from our expectation that model sizes are going to drastically increase, the number of users for all these things are going to drastically increase, and the context themselves.
zh: 我想说说我们的解决方案，以及我们正在尝试的做法，一方面是基于我们的预期：模型规模将会急剧增大，所有这些东西的用户数量将会急剧增加，还有上下文本身。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two, three years ago, the typical context links were on the order of 8,000 to 64,000 tokens.
zh: 两三年前，典型的上下文长度（links）在 8000 到 64000 token 的量级。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then it got up to 128, 256.

speaker: Unknown
en: A million token context links are the norm now in terms of what the models support.
zh: 一百万 token 的上下文长度（links）现在已经成为模型所支持的常态。

zh: 现在,在很多事情上我信任 Astra 远超过信任我自己,但我仍然要提示它去做事情,也许它会自主运行 12 个小时或三天。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the next big leap is when I trust a model running on my laptop or on my phone.
zh: 我认为下一个大飞跃,是当我信任一个跑在我笔记本或手机上的模型,

speaker: Unknown
en: to prompt the smarter models to do even more wider set of tasks.
zh: 去提示更聪明的模型去做范围更广得多的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we look at the data economy that powers the larger models which you believe in, we see Mercor, we see Surge hitting $3 billion in revenue.
zh: 当我们审视为大型模型提供动力的数据经济——你相信这一点——我们看到 Mercor,我们看到 Surge 营收达到 30 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: How big do these companies become?
zh: 这些公司会变得多大?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because Anthropic and OpenAI are $4 to $5 trillion businesses, say, feasible.
zh: 因为 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 说是 4 到 5 万亿美元的生意,这是可行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's wholly feasible, isn't it, that Mercor and Surge are $200 billion businesses, which serve both Frontier Labs and some of the world's biggest enterprises building their own models?
zh: Mercor 和 Surge 成为 2000 亿美元的生意,同时服务于前沿实验室和一些在构建自己模型的世界最大企业,这完全是可行的,不是吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think my only skepticism there is on there being vertical integration by the frontier labs.
zh: 我在那方面唯一的怀疑是前沿实验室的垂直整合。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the reason that hasn't happened is because Anthropic and OpenAI have better uses of their capital and mental power, et cetera, than doing all of the, you know, scale AI, Mercor, et cetera, work.
zh: 我认为之所以还没发生,是因为 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 有比去做所有那些 scale AI、Mercor 之类工作更好的资本和脑力用途等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that won't always exist.
zh: 但我认为这种情况不会永远存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And let's say that GPT-7 or 8 could be an effective replacement for Sam Altman in terms of being able to manage a large business, why they wouldn't just have agents be taking over those tasks.
zh: 假如说 GPT-7 或 8 能在管理一个大企业方面有效地替代 Sam Altman,为什么他们不让智能体接管那些任务呢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we leave, I'd like to finish on a tone of optimism.
zh: 在结束之前,我想以乐观的基调收尾。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you most excited about today that you think the world does not spend enough time on that we should spend time on?
zh: 今天你最兴奋的是什么,你认为世界在它身上花的时间不够,而我们应该花时间?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm very sympathetic to the problems that I think the smarter set of the AI alignment, AI safety community are when it comes to thinking about how do you align incentives?
zh: 我非常认同我认为 AI 对齐、AI 安全圈子里更聪明的那些人所关注的问题,即如何对齐激励?

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people just talk about AI alignment being a problem.
zh: 很多人只是把 AI 对齐当作一个问题来谈论。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a key part of that is human alignment.
zh: 我认为其中一个关键部分是人类对齐。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, how do we, society, human race, align ourselves to have a good outcome that I think will be empowered by artificial intelligence?
zh: 就是,我们、社会、人类,如何对齐我们自己以获得一个好的结局,我认为我们将被人工智能赋能。

speaker: Unknown
en: We discussed a bunch of the different problems that we're facing geopolitically and socially and how these different things are handled.
zh: 我们讨论了很多我们在地缘政治和社会层面面临的各种问题,以及这些不同的事情如何被处理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think a lot of smart people are doing good work on the AI alignment problem and thinking through how we solve that.
zh: 我认为很多聪明人正在 AI 对齐问题上做很好的工作,思考我们如何解决它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they may be gated in what can be done there if we don't get better human alignment on
zh: 但如果我们在人类对齐上没有做得更好,他们在那方面能做的事可能会被卡住,

speaker: Unknown
en: Be it regulatory frameworks and energy production, where we're going to put the data centers, et cetera, et cetera.
zh: 无论是监管框架和能源生产、我们要把数据中心放在哪里,等等等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think framing it as this being a similar sort of technical problem that smart people can work and reason through will hopefully get more people thinking about it that way.
zh: 我认为把它框定为一个类似的、聪明人可以去工作和推理解决的技术问题,希望能让更多人那样去思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think a core element that gets discounted by, I think, a lot of people in that sphere, there are a lot of economic factors.
zh: 而且我认为有一个被那个圈子里很多人低估的核心要素,就是有很多经济因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's the economic factors that actually will drive real decision-making and actions.
zh: 而我认为真正驱动实际决策和行动的,正是这些经济因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we don't look at it from a rational, self-interested actors and all these different things, you're just not going to make progress.
zh: 如果我们不从理性的、自利的行动者以及所有这些不同的角度来看待它,你就是不会取得进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thomas, this has been the most varied discussion ever from education on unbelievable infrastructure evolution to Dario and Sam.
zh: Thomas,这是有史以来话题最广泛的一次讨论,从教育到令人难以置信的基础设施演进,再到 Dario 和 Sam。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are a star.
zh: 你是一颗明星。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much for joining me today.
zh: 非常感谢你今天加入我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much, Harry.
zh: 非常感谢,Harry。

speaker: Unknown
en: But before we leave you today, the best model for your application might not exist yet.
zh: 但在今天离开之前,适合你应用的最好模型可能还不存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: The most ambitious AI teams are training open models to beat the frontier in their domain.
zh: 最有雄心的 AI 团队正在训练开源模型,以在他们的领域击败前沿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now on November the 3rd in San Francisco, Forge, by fireworks, brings those teams together.
zh: 现在,11 月 3 日在旧金山,Fireworks 举办的 Forge 把这些团队聚集在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: People like Jensen Huang, CEO of NVIDIA, Michelle Katasta, President and Head of AI at Replit.
zh: 有 NVIDIA 的 CEO Jensen Huang 这样的人,还有 Replit 的总裁兼 AI 负责人 Michelle Katasta,

speaker: Unknown
en: Lin Quao, CEO of Fireworks, and more to hear how AI leaders are taking control of their differentiation, margins, and roadmap by owning their intelligence.
zh: 还有 Fireworks 的 CEO Lin Quao 等更多人,来听 AI 领导者们如何通过拥有自己的智能来掌控自己的差异化、利润率和路线图。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn how they're building it with inference, training, and intelligent routing.
zh: 了解他们如何用推理、训练和智能路由来构建它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Forge is free to attend, but space is limited.
zh: Forge 免费参加,但名额有限。

speaker: Unknown
en: Apply today at fireworks.ai forward slash forge.
zh: 今天就在 fireworks.ai forward slash forge 申请。

speaker: Unknown
en: While Fireworks AI powers product intelligence, Asana keeps the work moving.
zh: 在 Fireworks AI 驱动产品智能的同时,Asana 让工作持续运转。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most companies have tried AI, most aren't seeing results.
zh: 大多数公司都尝试过 AI,大多数却没有看到结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not because AI doesn't work, it's because AI hasn't reached the workflows yet.
zh: 不是因为 AI 不行,而是因为 AI 还没有触及工作流。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the gap Asana is built to close.
zh: 这正是 Asana 为之而生的要弥补的差距。

speaker: Unknown
en: Asana is the operating system for human agent teams, your easy button for AI productivity across every team.
zh: Asana 是人类加智能体团队的操作系统,是你在每个团队实现 AI 生产力的轻松按钮。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ready-to-go AI teammates, pre-built for marketing, ops, and IT.
zh: 开箱即用的 AI 队友,为市场、运营和 IT 预先构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: No prompt engineering, no setup, they show up where the work is happening, already onboarded, in your workflows, ready to deliver.
zh: 无需提示词工程,无需设置,它们出现在工作发生的地方,已经完成入职,在你的工作流里,随时准备交付。

speaker: Unknown
en: With Asana, your whole company can work on the same plan towards the same goal, whether you're a team of 10 or a team of 10,000.
zh: 有了 Asana,无论你是 10 人团队还是 1 万人团队,整个公司都可以围绕同一个计划朝着同一个目标工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Asana, where humans and agents workflow together.
zh: Asana,人类与智能体协作工作流的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Try it at asana.com, that's A-S-A-N-A dot com.
zh: 试试 asana.com,网址是 A-S-A-N-A 点 com。

speaker: Unknown
en: While Asana organizes the work, Superhuman speeds up the day.
zh: Asana 负责整理工作,Superhuman 则为一天提速。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I be honest with you for a second?
zh: 我能跟你说句实话吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's what my week actually looks like.
zh: 这才是我一周的真实样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Back-to-back meetings all day, and the real pressure builds up in the gaps between them.
zh: 一整天连轴转的会议,真正的压力是在会议之间的间隙里积攒起来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll come out of six founder meetings with a whole stack of follow-ups waiting, and my inbox is hundreds of messages, and somewhere in there is the one thing that really matters, which I always tell my mother is her.
zh: 我从六场创始人会议里出来,堆着一大摞待跟进事项,收件箱里有几百封邮件,而其中某处藏着那件真正重要的事——我总是跟我母亲说,那个人是她。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've tried AI tools for this, but they always lived in another tab.
zh: 我试过用 AI 工具来解决这个问题,但它们总是活在另一个标签页里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd have to stop, go find it, paste in the context, write the perfect prompt.
zh: 我得停下来,找到它,把上下文粘贴进去,写出一个完美的提示词。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was just enough friction that it never really stuck.
zh: 摩擦刚好大到让它始终没能真正留下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Superhuman Go from the makers of Grammarly, totally different.
zh: Grammarly 的出品方推出的 Superhuman Go,完全不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's right there where you need it, when you need it, in the doc, when I'm reading, the email I'm writing, when a thread gets dense, I highlight it and ask Go to pull out what matters without losing my place.
zh: 它就在你需要它的地方,在你需要它的时候——在文档里、在我阅读时、在我写邮件时;当一个帖子变得信息密集,我选中它,让 Go 提取重点,而不会让我失去阅读位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: And after a run of back-to-backs,
zh: 而在一连串连轴会议之后,

speaker: Unknown
en: I ask what was actually decided and Go turns it into clear action items or drafts, the reply I need to send.
zh: 我问实际决定了什么,Go 会把它变成清晰的操作项或草稿,写出我需要发送的回复。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's already up to speed and I'm always the one in control.
zh: 它已经完全进入状态,而掌控权始终在我手里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Try Superhuman Go from the makers of Grammarly and find out more at superhuman.com.
zh: 试试 Grammarly 出品方推出的 Superhuman Go,到 superhuman.com 了解更多。
